title: Responses API round‑trip reconciliation and loss scorecard
creator: Ayesha Kumar
description:
Goal: Design and implement a reconciliation engine and scorecard for measuring behavioral loss when mapping external OpenAI Responses API artifacts onto Redwood's internal protocol. This ticket covers defining a loss scoring model, building round‑trip tests that exercise streaming + tool calling + structured output, and creating dashboards that surface high‑impact deltas for product/eng review.

Motivation: Customers depend on parity when migrating from OpenAI Responses to Redwood. Prior audits surfaced subtle invariants (token provenance, toolcall framing, trailing stream events, structured field renaming) that lead to silent regressions. Rather than ad‑hoc fixes, we need an automated way to quantify "how much" mapping changes output, prioritize deltas by customer surface area, and provide deterministic round‑trip checks for future merges.

Scope & deliverables:
- Define a loss scoring rubric (semantic drift, structural loss, event-order divergence, token provenance breaks).
- Implement a reconciliation engine that runs pairwise comparisons: OpenAI Responses canonical trace vs Redwood-mapped trace. The engine will produce a normalized delta report and loss score.
- Build a synthetic workload harness that can exercise streaming+toolcall+structured outputs (including partial chunking and late-arriving tool results).
- Add telemetry hooks to capture deltas in canary traffic and wire to a dashboard with actionable filters (model, endpoint, customer tag, severity).
- Create a runbook documenting common delta classes, recommended mitigations, and a CI gating rule for high-severity regressions.
tasks: Draft loss rubric and weighting (semantic, structural, ordering, timing, token_provenance)
Prototype roundtrip comparator that tokenizes and aligns stream events
Create synthetic harness to generate combinations of streaming + function/tool call sequences
Instrument runtime to emit canonicalized traces for canary traffic
Ship a Grafana dashboard + alert for loss_score > 0.35 on production canaries
Author runbook and CI gating proposal for release engineering
acceptance_criteria: Loss rubric doc reviewed by PM and Applied ML
Comparator prototype covers at least 8 classes of deltas from the delta taxonomy
Synthetic harness can reliably reproduce at least 3 previously observed customer regressions
Dashboard surfaces per-endpoint and per-model loss_score and is queryable by customer tag
A CI check fails builds when new commits increase loss_score on the representative test bundle by >10%
comments: 2025-02-12 Marco Liu: Kickoff — sketched the initial rubric. Focused on measurable signals rather than prose. Need to loop in Applied ML for semantic scoring model.

2025-02-14 Ayesha Kumar: Added prototype comparator notes; deciding whether alignment should be token-level or event-level. Token-level gives precision for provenance bugs but is more brittle across tokenizers.

2025-02-17 Sofia Ortega (Applied ML): Reviewed rubric draft — proposed using embedding-based semantic distance for 'semantic drift' and Levenshtein-like metrics for structural loss. Recommend weighting semantic drift lower for short outputs.

2025-02-19 Marco Liu: Ran roundtrip against the 'tool-late-arrival' fixture. Comparator flagged ordering divergence and missing 'tool_result.id' fields. Created GitHub issue: github.com/redwood-inference/resp-compat/issues/142
2025-02-22 PM review (Liam O'Neill): Requested that the dashboard include a per-customer traffic weight so we can triage regressions by exposed user impact rather than raw counts.
2025-02-25 Marco Liu: Instrumentation merged to canary (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4687). Initial canary traces start appearing in the new 'resp-parity' index.
2025-02-25 Note: We'll run a 2-week canary period, then evaluate if gating thresholds need tightening.
risks: False positives from tokenization differences could flood alerts — mitigate by silencing low-severity token diffs and grouping by semantic impact
Performance overhead of trace export could increase tail latency on canaries; will sample 1% of requests initially
Weighting scheme may over prioritize rare but noisy regressions — will use traffic-weighted scoring
test_plan: Unit tests for comparator alignment logic
Golden roundtrip fixtures covering streaming-only, toolcall-only, and mixed sequences
Fuzz test harness that mutates ordering and partial streams to validate robustness
Canary run for 2 weeks with daily dashboard reviews
rollout_plan: Merge comparator to staging, run full sweep against representative model set
Enable trace export on 1% of production requests for 2 weeks
If loss_score spike < threshold, expand to 10% and enable CI gating on representative suite
If high-severity regressions found, block release trains and trigger mitigation playbook
